module.title: Receivables: classification, loss estimates and evidence
module.goal: Challenge a receivables allowance using a supplied loss matrix and a documented evidence boundary.
module.scope: IFRS 9 foundation. Matrix rates are fictional assumptions, not prescribed loss rates. Full staging, discounting, hedge accounting and detailed asset classification are outside this case; local FRS 102 policies require their own assessment.

sections.title: 1. Classify before calculating
paragraphs: IFRS 9 classification considers how financial assets are managed and their contractual cash-flow features. An account name alone cannot settle the measurement category. The standard also includes expected-credit-loss impairment requirements.

Original review task: ask for the receivable contract, how balances are managed and the approved accounting policy. A balance labelled “customer” may still have unusual settlement terms. This case assumes the classification and applicable impairment approach have already been reviewed so you can focus on the estimate.
sections.supportPt: O nome da conta não define a classificação. Confira contrato, gestão e política antes do cálculo.

sections.title: 2. Read the supplied estimate
paragraphs: Original fictional matrix: current balances 800 at an assumed 1% loss rate give 8; overdue balances 200 at an assumed 10% give 20. Total gross receivables are 1,000, allowance 28 and net carrying amount 972. These supplied rates are teaching inputs.

A neat calculation does not validate the rates. Ask what information supports the grouping and rates, what changed since the last review, and whether customer-specific information contradicts the pooled estimate. Do not treat every current invoice as risk-free or every overdue invoice as wholly lost.
sections.supportPt: A conta fecha em 28, mas a taxa ainda precisa de evidência. Vencimento e perda não são a mesma coisa.

sections.title: 3. Explain an allowance movement
paragraphs: Original bridge: opening allowance 25 plus expense 8 less an approved write-off of 5 gives closing allowance 28. The movement in the allowance balance is only 3, while the expense is 8. There are no recoveries, exchange movements or other entries in this exercise.

Request the write-off authorisation and underlying invoice list. A write-off is not a bank receipt, and a lower gross balance does not by itself prove collection. Keep the matrix total and the movement schedule as two independent checks.
sections.supportPt: Saldo e despesa diferem quando há baixa. Concilie a matriz e o roll-forward separadamente.

sections.title: 4. Give a review conclusion
paragraphs: Original controller response: the arithmetic supports an allowance of 28 under the supplied assumptions, but the reasonableness of the rates still needs documented support. The allowance expense is 8 after allowing for the write-off of 5. Assign the credit owner to supply the loss-history and current-customer review.

For an Irish statutory output under a different framework, confirm its applicable requirements and policy choices. A correct IFRS group calculation is not automatic permission to copy that entry into every local ledger.
sections.supportPt: Separe cálculo correto de estimativa validada e confirme a base da entrega local.

terms.meaning: Amount reducing a receivable carrying value for estimated losses.
Removal of an approved uncollectible balance in this case.
terms.example: The bridge includes a write-off of 5.

terms.meaning: Assumed loss proportion for a defined group.
Combining balances with relevant shared characteristics.
terms.example: Challenge whether one group hides a specific issue.
The roll-forward explains expense versus balance change.

visual.title: Receivables: classification, loss estimates and evidence — decision map
visual.note: Original fictional exercise; not a live calculation or measured learner result.
visual.question: Is an allowance increase of 3 necessarily the expense?
visual.answer: No. The approved write-off means expense is 8 in the supplied bridge.

caseStudy.title: Receivables: classification, loss estimates and evidence — applied case
scenario: Fictional matrix: 800 at 1%; 200 at 10%. Rates and classification are supplied assumptions.
Opening allowance 25, approved write-off 5, closing allowance per matrix 28. No other movements.
A manager says the expense must be 3 because the balance increased by 3.
caseStudy.task: Calculate the matrix, reconcile the expense and state one unresolved estimation question.
caseStudy.modelAnswer: Allowance is 8 + 20 = 28; net receivables are 972. Expense is 8 because 25 + 8 - 5 = 28. The balance increase of 3 is not the expense. Ask for support for the assumed loss rates and review any customer-specific contrary evidence.
reviewChecks: No claim that rates are mandated or validated.
caseStudy.transfer: Change one group rate and explain whether arithmetic or estimation judgement changed.

checkpoint.prompt: What is the expense in the case?
Are the rates prescribed by this lesson?
Can the account name alone decide classification?

options: A balance was removed under the case approval
checkpoint.explanation: It is not evidence of a cash receipt.

practiceExercises.question: Overdue balances 150 use a supplied 8% rate. Calculate the assumed loss.
practiceExercises.explanation: Arithmetic does not validate the 8% assumption.

practiceExercises.question: Opening allowance 40; expense 9; approved write-off 6. Find closing allowance.
practiceExercises.explanation: A write-off and an expense play different roles.

practiceExercises.question: A manager sets every current receivable to zero expected loss because nothing is overdue. Challenge the reasoning.
hints: Ask for evidence of expected losses.
practiceExercises.answer: Current status alone does not establish zero loss; review the appropriate method and supporting information.
practiceExercises.explanation: Do not replace judgement with one ageing label.

sources.label: IFRS Foundation — IFRS 9
sources.supports: Classification by business model and contractual cash flows; expected-credit-loss impairment. Cases are simplified original illustrations, not a complete valuation model.

professorGuide.opening: Ask why an allowance balance change may differ from expense.
professorGuide.whenCorrect: Ask what would change if a new customer-specific fact contradicts the pooled rate.
professorGuide.whenUncertain: Ask which supplied fact is missing or unclear. Offer the first case hint, then invite another attempt.
professorGuide.whenMisconception: If the learner answers 3 as expense, walk through the approved write-off, then let them rebuild the bridge.
professorGuide.whenSelfCorrected: Use the corrected answer, not the abandoned phrase, as the current response. Ask one transfer question.
professorGuide.whenAskedForAnswer: Provide a concise explanation and one worked step; invite an optional fresh attempt without claiming independent mastery.
professorGuide.evidenceBoundary: Use only actual session evidence if this guide is separately integrated. Never consume local drafts or checkpoint results. Do not infer pronunciation/acoustic fluency from text, technical mastery from a phrase, or a CEFR level from one task.
